usageNotes: Triggers an in-cluster live or offline migration of a QEMU VM on the specified PDM-managed remote; the only required body param is `target` (destination node name). Returns a remote UPID string representing the async task — poll that UPID via the task-status endpoint to detect completion or failure. Use `online: true` to migrate a running VM with minimal downtime, and set `with-local-disks: true` plus `target-storage` mappings when the VM has disks on node-local storage that must follow the VM to the target node.

examples.summary: Online migrate a running VM (VMID 105) to node pve-node2 on remote prod-cluster, carrying its local disk to the target's local-lvm storage

destructiveReason: Migration moves the VM's runtime state and disk data off the source node; if it fails mid-transfer the VM may be left in a degraded or locked state requiring manual recovery.
tips: The return value is a remote UPID (min 42 chars) — treat it as an opaque task handle and poll task status; do not assume the migration is done when the POST returns.
Omitting `online` (or setting it false) requires the VM to be stopped before migration; the call will fail on a running VM unless `online: true` is passed.
Setting `migration-type: insecure` disables SSH tunnel encryption and can significantly increase throughput on isolated internal networks where latency matters.
`force: true` is needed when the VM has passthrough/local devices (e.g. PCI passthrough); without it the API will reject the request outright.
Specify `migration-network` as a CIDR (e.g. 10.0.10.0/24) to force migration traffic onto a dedicated storage/migration VLAN instead of the management interface.
The `node` param identifies the *source* node when the remote is a cluster and the VM's current node is ambiguous; omit it if PDM can infer the source automatically.
